objective: Keep every terminal the user explicitly closes gone after restart while preserving every terminal the user leaves open
requirements: A sidebar X close removes only the selected terminal and records its durable close identity
A pane X close removes only the selected terminal and records its durable close identity
Typing /exit removes only the selected terminal and records its durable close identity
Restart never restores an explicitly closed terminal
Restart restores every terminal the user did not close, without killing or hiding it
Installed dock-launched runtime evidence proves the behavior across repeated restart cycles
The user remains the only authority that can approve the final visible result
knownFailures: Previously closed terminals returned after restart
Earlier recovery cleanup could close terminals the user had not closed
Source-only checks did not prove the installed dock-launched runtime
outOfScope: Changing daemon ownership or killing background PTYs during UI restart
Treating a process kill performed outside the app as a user close action
Closing or approving the goal without explicit user approval

sure.rootCause: Recovery previously lacked a single durable, user-authored close decision shared by every close route.
sure.research: Focused route contracts, workspace persistence checks, daemon restore checks, installed release checks, and live visual evidence cover sidebar close, pane close, slash exit, restart, and untouched-terminal survival.
sure.fix: Record explicit close intent by terminal identity and filter only those identities during durable restore; keep daemon-owned sessions alive unless the user explicitly closes them.
sure.sideEffects: The change is scoped to close/recovery state and its regression gates; unrelated dirty work and untouched sessions are preserved.
